note: Branch pairs written by independent Claude Code agents from the same base (7950d86). Tags point at each agent's original commit. Ground-truth labels are human judgements; the reasoning is stated for each pair.

scenarios.name: fee_x_cents
scenarios.why: #2 writes the fee threshold/amount in float dollars and calls round_money; #1 makes every amount integer cents and removes round_money. Combined, the fee is never charged (995 cents is not < 15.00) or the code crashes.

scenarios.name: save10_x_cents
scenarios.why: #3 keeps SAVE10's minimum as 40.00 dollars and uses round_money; with #1's integer cents the minimum becomes 40 cents (discount on almost every order) or the code crashes.

scenarios.name: save10_x_fee
scenarios.why: Both add a line to quote() (textual conflict) but the features are independent: the fee applies under $15, SAVE10 only at $40+, and both keep tax on the (discounted) subtotal excluding the fee.

scenarios.name: region_x_cents
scenarios.why: #4 only adds an IN-MH rate; #1 keeps rates as fractions and applies them to cents, so IN-MH still taxes 18%. (#4's own tests are written in dollars and will fail on the merge: a test-representation clash, not a behavior one.)

scenarios.name: region_x_fee
scenarios.why: New tax region vs small-order fee: no shared behavior.

scenarios.name: currency_x_cents
scenarios.why: #5 adds a currency field to charges; #1 changes amount units in orders/pricing. Charges already took integer cents, so neither intent depends on the other.

scenarios.name: currency_x_region
scenarios.why: Payments vs tax rates: no shared code or behavior.

scenarios.name: currency_x_save10
scenarios.why: #3 passes an optional code through place_order; #5 adds an optional currency to charge(): independent.
